desc:
An email and SMS performance report explains what your messages earned, what they missed and what to do next. Ecom Swift LLC reads the numbers in your own tool and writes them up in plain language, so you do not have to decode the dashboard.

## What is an email and SMS performance report?

An email and SMS performance report is a written review of how your campaigns and automated flows performed over a set period. It shows clicks, revenue, list growth, unsubscribes and complaints, compares them with the previous period and finishes with clear next steps.

Raw dashboards show many numbers but rarely say which matter. A report picks out the few that explain what happened and why.

## Why reading the numbers matters

Sending without review is guessing. A store may send for months without knowing that one flow earns most of its email revenue, that one segment ignores every campaign or that a certain subject style causes unsubscribes. Without a review, effort goes to the wrong places.

A report also warns you early. A rise in complaints, a drop in list growth or a flow that suddenly stopped can be fixed quickly if noticed quickly. Reviewing results each period keeps decisions based on what your own customers did, not on general advice.

Open rates need care. Privacy features in mail apps can open messages automatically, so opens may overstate real interest. We lean on clicks, revenue and replies, and say clearly where a number is uncertain.

## What a good report contains

- A short summary on the first page, written for a busy owner.
- Results for each campaign: sends, clicks, revenue attributed by your tool and unsubscribes.
- Results for each automated flow, separated from one-off campaigns.
- Best and weakest sends, with a simple reason for each.
- List growth and loss, including new signups and unsubscribes.
- Complaint and bounce figures, since they affect inbox placement.
- SMS results next to email, when both are in use.
- Comparison with the last period, so trends are visible.
- Notes on what could distort a number, such as a sale week or a tracking gap.
- Specific next steps: what to stop, keep, repeat and test.

## How we produce it

We pull data from your own account for the period you choose. Then we check it for gaps, such as flows with no revenue tracking or campaigns sent to unusual groups. We explain each figure in everyday words, group the findings and write the next steps in order of value.

The Basic package covers one month of campaigns with a best and weakest send and three next steps. Standard adds flows, revenue per flow and campaign, list growth and a comparison with the previous month. Premium covers a quarter, adds SMS, results by segment, a stop-keep-test list and a review call. Add-ons include an extra month, a flow audit and a presentation version for team meetings. Attributed revenue is the tool's own estimate, and we say so.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Compare periods of similar length and season.
- Judge flows and campaigns separately.
- Change only one or two things after each report so you can see what helped.
- Keep notes on what changed between reports.
- Ask why a number moved before celebrating it.

**Avoid:**
- Treating open rate as proof of interest.
- Comparing a holiday month with a quiet one.
- Changing five things at once and learning nothing.
- Ignoring unsubscribes because the revenue looks good.
- Copying another store's results as your target.

## Who it is for

An owner who sends every week and has never looked at the results will gain a clear picture. A manager who must report to a founder or client can use the presentation version. A store that changed tools or strategy can check whether the change helped.

## What we need from you

Tell us the tool and the period to review, and add us as a collaborator, staff or team user with view access to reports. We never need passwords. Share any dates of sales or changes that might affect the figures. You stay the owner of your account, and the report is yours to keep.
